newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa truth body mulls summoning Winnie Mandela.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa truth body mulls summoning Winnie Mandela.

text.p: South Africa's truth commission into apartheid-era crimes has yet to decide whether to summon Winnie Madikizela-Mandela in connection with two missing children, a commission investigator said on Wednesday.
"No subpoena has been issued, the commission is still completing its investigation," Yasmin Sooka told reporters.
She was commenting on newspaper reports this week that bodyguards of Madikizela-Mandela, divorced wife of President Nelson Mandela, had thrown the bodies of children down disused mine shafts.
The newspapers quoted unnamed commission sources as saying a former colleague of Madikizela-Mandela had provided a map showing the mine shafts.
But Sooka, who is heading the investigation into Madikizela-Mandela, said: "To my knowledge, no such map has been received."

Sooka said early in May it was "more than likely" that the president's former wife would be subpoenaed to tell the commission what she knew about the disappearance of two black children in Soweto township during the 1980s.

During those years Madikizela-Mandela had an entourage of bodyguards dubbed "the Mandela United Football Club" who township residents said conducted a reign of terror, abducting and beating people on suspicion they were police informers.
The head of the club, Jerry Richardson, was jailed for life after being convicted of murdering 14-year-old Stompie Seipei. Madikizela-Mandela was fined for taking part in the abduction of the boy.
